name: Alhambra, Palacio de Comares and Palacio de los Leones

dates.altered: The Palace of Charles V driven into the south side of the Comares palace from 1527; extensive 19th- and 20th-century restoration under the Patronato.
dates.note: The node's exemplar gives 1333-1391 under Yusuf I and Muhammad V and dates the row 1391. The Generalife infobox on the same site prints '14th century' for the neighbouring estate.

refs.title: Alhambra, Generalife and Albayzín, Granada; UNESCO reference no. 314, inscribed 1984, extended 1994
refs.note: The reference number, the official name and both session dates were read in the Generalife article's World Heritage infobox, which names the same property. The inscription covers three things -- the Alhambra, the Generalife and the Albayzin quarter -- so the number is not an identity for this palace.

survey.prepared: No revision date was printed in the extract. AN ENCYCLOPEDIA ARTICLE AND NOT A REGISTER.

quotes.text: , a courtyard measuring 23 to 23.5 metres wide and 36.6 metres long, with its long axis aligned roughly north-to-south. At the middle, aligned with the main axis of the court, is a wide reflective pool. The pool measures 34 metres long and 7,10 metres wide.
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, section on the Court of the Myrtles. THE SPAN BEGINS WITH A COMMA: the subject of the sentence is a wikilink the extractor dropped, so the words before the comma were not returned and are not invented here. The pool's width is printed with a comma decimal separator, '7,10 metres', and is left as it stands.

quotes.text: It is accessed by passing through the Sala de la Barca, a wide rectangular hall behind the northern portico of the court. The Hall of the Ambassadors is a square chamber measuring 11.3 metres per side and rising to a height of 18.2 metres.
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, section on the Salón de los Embajadores in the Comares Tower

quotes.text: The ceiling is made of 8017 interlinked pieces of wood that form an abstract
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, same section; THE SPAN ENDS MID-SENTENCE where the extract's returned chunk ends, and no continuation is supplied

measurements.name: court_width_ft
measurements.note: A band, not a figure: the article prints two numbers for the width of the Court of the Myrtles and chooses neither, so no value is parsed. 23 m is 75.5 ft and 23.5 m is 77.1 ft.

measurements.name: court_length_ft
measurements.note: Converted at 3.28084 ft/m. Against the printed width band this makes the court between 1.56 and 1.59 times as long as it is wide.

measurements.name: court_pool_length_ft
measurements.note: The node's own description calls this 'a slab of water thirty-four metres long', which is this figure.

measurements.name: court_pool_width_ft
measurements.note: Read as 7.10 m; the source prints a comma decimal separator.

measurements.name: hall_width_ft
measurements.note: The Hall of the Ambassadors is square, so this is both its width and its depth.

measurements.name: ceiling_height_ft
measurements.note: Floor to the crown of the domed ceiling of the Hall of the Ambassadors -- the largest room in the Alhambra and not a domestic ceiling height.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. Two of the three quotes are truncated by the extractor rather than by choice and each says where and why; the first begins after a dropped wikilink and the third ends mid-sentence. No word has been added to either.
